title: Never Curb Your Enthusiasm
html:
In this week’s MondayMotivator:

  • Enthusiasm is crucial for a fulfilling and exciting life.
  • Enthusiasm is contagious and impacts others positively.
  • Seize the day, infuse magic, and be proactive for a great life.

Do you feel something is missing in your life? Or you're worn out and tired? Your batteries likely need recharging, and the weather isn't helping if you live in Auckland.

However, it might be that you are suffering from negative association or negative self-talk. This is usually from associating with and listening to negative people with limiting views on life. Social media doesn't help.

Such behaviour dissipates your vitality and destroys your health. It doesn't have to be like this, yet many go through life with a great emptiness.

One of my keys to life is enthusiasm. The word enthusiasm means 'God within'. It's a feeling that opens the door to an exciting future full of opportunities.

Enthusiasm means to be on fire, to be excited about life.

You need to feel excited about what you do, or else you need to change what you are doing. Or your approach to what you are doing if you can't change it quickly. Your enthusiasm will become contagious and affect other people.

What differentiates the popular type of person from the not-so-popular type? It is the excitement that creates the magic between them and other people. Others feed off your energy and enthusiasm.

Each day when you arise, think of the Latin phrase, 'Carpe Diem,' seize the day. Make it fulfilling. As Seth Godin said, make it remarkable by putting some magic in your life.

Get excited and think I will seize the day and make it great! I will be active, energetic and ready for the opportunity and the chance to help others. I will become excited about what I do and transfer that magic to others.

Life is too short to be dull. Find something to be enthusiastic about. Something you're doing now or looking forward to doing later. That feeling will power you with unstoppable energy through the days, weeks, and years ahead.
